topic: The Daily Habit Ep 6: today's 7 stories (India tops ChatGPT, says OpenAI; Marvell to buy Lumentum, ~$115B; Apple's inventory jumps 154.3%; UPI tops 25 billion in a month; Karpathy's build-your-own ChatGPT; Startup funding falls 47.5%; Anthropic IPO: up to $3.5B in Japan)
angle_hint: An episode digest carousel: slide 1 a bold hook naming the biggest story and that there are 7 stories today; then one stat, compare or fact slide per story for the first five stories in the episode's order (each with its own source); a close slide inviting people to watch the full episode for all of them.

facts.text: India's ChatGPT user base has doubled since January 2026, per Singh.
In February 2026, Sam Altman said India had 100 million weekly active ChatGPT users, making it ChatGPT's second-largest user base after the United States.
OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT ads in India to support free and lower-priced access. Early advertisers include Tanishq, Fastrack, Tata Neu and Shaadi.com.
OpenAI is expected to announce UPI and payments-related features in the coming weeks.
Marvell has agreed to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock deal with an enterprise value of $115 billion including debt; equity value is about $80 billion.
Lumentum shareholders get 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share.
Nvidia invested $2 billion in Lumentum in March and, later that month, $2 billion in Marvell.
The deal is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approval.

After closing, Marvell stockholders would own about 67% and Lumentum stockholders about 33% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis; Marvell expects line of sight to more than $1 billion in annual run-rate cost synergies.
Apple's inventory grew 154.3% year over year, from $5.72 billion in Q4 2025 to $14.54 billion in Q4 fiscal 2026.
Inventory rose 31.1% quarter over quarter, from $11.09 billion in Q3.
CEO John Ternus called memory pricing "unprecedented" and expects even higher memory costs in the December quarter, and rising beyond that.
Apple forecasts a 45% to 46% gross margin for the December quarter, mainly due to memory costs, versus 47.9% in the September quarter.
Apple raised prices earlier this year on some Mac and iPad models (end of June) and iPhones (September); COO Sabih Khan did not rule out further device price increases.
UPI processed 25.47 billion transactions in October, the first month above 25 billion, worth Rs 31.53 lakh crore (NPCI data).
Volume rose 23% from 20.7 billion in October last year; value rose 16%.
Daily average was 822 million transactions (up from 802 million in September), worth about Rs 1.01 lakh crore a day.
Peak day was 9 October with 873 million payments.
September 2026 comparison: 24.07 billion transactions worth Rs 29.37 lakh crore, per NPCI data.

The leaderboard's fastest 'time to GPT-2' entry is 1.65 hours (March 14, 2026, 'autoresearch round 2'). The README says the speedrun script takes ~1.5 hours to run, and the first leaderboard entry was 3.04 hours.
It also runs on a single GPU (you'll wait 8 times longer), and there is a CPU-only / MPS install option.
Indian startups raised about $678 million in October 2026, per Entrackr's tally.
That is down about 47.5% from $1.29 billion in September.
Year-on-year, funding fell 60.8% from $1.73 billion in October 2025.
No startup raised $100 million or more; the biggest rounds were Tessolve ($75 million) and Even Healthcare ($50 million).
Early-stage: 79 deals worth $263 million; growth and late-stage: 20 deals worth $414.6 million; nine deals had undisclosed amounts.
Anthropic will sell up to 552.9 billion yen ($3.5 billion) worth of shares in Japan as part of its US public listing, a filing showed on Monday (Nov 2).
The new shares sold to Japanese investors will raise working capital and fund operating expenses and capital expenditure.
Mizuho Securities will manage the Japan share sale; Goldman Sachs, Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities and Morgan Stanley MUFG Securities are among firms handling subscription applications.
For comparison, Japanese investors got $2.2 billion of the $75 billion raised in SpaceX's June IPO, the largest ever.
The filing did not state overall offering size or valuation; Reuters has reported some investors have discussed a valuation of about $1.5 trillion.

cautions: The largest-market and doubling claims come from one OpenAI executive's statement via ET/Inc42. I found no independent confirmation and no exact current user number.
'Doubled' refers to the user base; the base metric isn't stated. Don't say it is 200 million weekly users.
The 100M figure is from Feb 2026 and ranked India second to the US then.
I did not open the ET original. The TechCrunch fact comes from search results, not a page I read.
$115B is enterprise value including debt; equity value is about $80B. Don't call it an $115B cheque.
A Lumentum internal email reportedly calls it about $100 billion, so say 'about $115B' and attribute it.
It's not done: closing is expected in H1 2028 and needs shareholder and regulatory approval.
Nvidia is a minority investor in both ($2B each) and isn't a party to the deal. Don't imply it brokered the deal.
The Activision ($68.7B) and Dell-EMC ($67B) comparisons come from TechCrunch, not the companies.
The SEC exhibit page was read only through a search summary, not opened in full.
Only one source (TechCrunch) was read; no independent second source was checked.
Apple has not announced new price hikes; Khan only did not rule them out.
